decks.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: For a pedestrian in a crosswalk, stop and stay stopped when the.
cards.back: For a pedestrian in a crosswalk, stop and stay stopped when the person is on your half of the road or approaching within one lane of that half. The handbook defines the half as the lanes carrying one direction of traffic.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The crosswalk stopping duty applies during left and right turns, before moving.
cards.back: The crosswalk stopping duty applies during left and right turns, before moving from a stop sign, and even with a green light when pedestrians are still crossing.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Stop for a pedestrian before entering the.
cards.back: Stop for a pedestrian before entering the road from an alley, driveway or private road.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Give a blind pedestrian using a white cane or.
cards.back: Give a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog the right of way when crossing the road.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: An intersection crosswalk may exist without painted markings, following the extension of.
cards.back: An intersection crosswalk may exist without painted markings, following the extension of the sidewalk across the street. A marked crosswalk can also be located midblock.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Do not block a crosswalk; stop before it at a.
cards.back: Do not block a crosswalk; stop before it at a red light or stop sign so pedestrians can cross safely.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: At an unsignalized crosswalk, stop for a pedestrian on your directional.
cards.back: At an unsignalized crosswalk, stop for a pedestrian on your directional half of the road or approaching within one lane of it.

decks.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Check both roadsides for pedestrians near intersections, turns, schools, parks and bus.
cards.back: Check both roadsides for pedestrians near intersections, turns, schools, parks and bus stops, and look behind for people before backing in a driveway or parking area.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Before a permitted right turn on red, stop fully before the crosswalk.
cards.back: Before a permitted right turn on red, stop fully before the crosswalk. After checking left for traffic, also check the passenger side for someone crossing ahead.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A stopped vehicle on a multilane road may hide a pedestrian in.
cards.back: A stopped vehicle on a multilane road may hide a pedestrian in a crosswalk. Approach with extreme caution rather than assuming the next lane is clear.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: When stopping for a crosswalk on a multilane road, the handbook recommends.
cards.back: When stopping for a crosswalk on a multilane road, the handbook recommends at least ten feet of space before the crossing so drivers in adjacent lanes can see the pedestrian.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Entering or leaving a driveway, alley or parking garage requires.
cards.back: Entering or leaving a driveway, alley or parking garage requires stopping before the sidewalk and waiting until pedestrians have passed.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Before turning left into a driveway, wait for pedestrians crossing.
cards.back: Before turning left into a driveway, wait for pedestrians crossing its sidewalk portion as well as an opening in oncoming traffic.

decks.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Pedestrians lack the vehicle occupants' protection, and higher vehicle speed.
cards.back: Pedestrians lack the vehicle occupants' protection, and higher vehicle speed increases the risk of a serious or fatal pedestrian injury.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Expect bicycles on roads and watch for them.
cards.back: Expect bicycles on roads and watch for them rather than assuming only larger vehicles will appear.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The handbook allows bicyclists on Georgia roads other than interstates and.
cards.back: The handbook allows bicyclists on Georgia roads other than interstates and similar limited-access highways, and gives them use of a full lane.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A bicyclist is not required to use an available bicycle.
cards.back: A bicyclist is not required to use an available bicycle lane. Yield to the rider as you would to another driver.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: When possible, establish eye contact with.
cards.back: When possible, establish eye contact with a bicyclist, especially near an intersection.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Allow room for a bicycle rider to avoid potholes or other.
cards.back: Allow room for a bicycle rider to avoid potholes or other defects; the handbook states a minimum passing clearance of three feet.

decks.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: When approaching a bicycle, act cautiously and move to a lane that.
cards.back: When approaching a bicycle, act cautiously and move to a lane that is not adjacent to the rider when road and traffic conditions make that possible.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: If changing lanes to pass a bicycle is impossible, unlawful or unsafe.
cards.back: If changing lanes to pass a bicycle is impossible, unlawful or unsafe, the handbook requires at least three feet of clearance throughout the pass.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Be ready for a bicycle rider to move unexpectedly, including when.
cards.back: Be ready for a bicycle rider to move unexpectedly, including when traffic has prevented the rider from reaching the usual left-turn position.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A rider at night may lack lights or reflectors. Dim.
cards.back: A rider at night may lack lights or reflectors. Dim the vehicle headlights for an oncoming bicycle rider to avoid glare.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Do not drive or park in a.
cards.back: Do not drive or park in a bicycle lane; that infrastructure is for bicycles.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A bicycle may pass a motor vehicle on the right when there.
cards.back: A bicycle may pass a motor vehicle on the right when there is a dedicated lane or enough shared-lane space and the move is safe.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Bicyclists use arm signals to.
cards.back: Bicyclists use arm signals to indicate a turn, slowing or stopping.

decks.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Motorcyclists share the traffic rights and responsibilities of other.
cards.back: Motorcyclists share the traffic rights and responsibilities of other drivers but are more physically exposed in a collision.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A motorcycle's smaller outline can make it appear farther away or slower.
cards.back: A motorcycle's smaller outline can make it appear farther away or slower than it is. Check again at intersections and check blind spots directly before changing lanes.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Give a motorcycle the full lane; do not.
cards.back: Give a motorcycle the full lane; do not share that lane while driving beside or passing it.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A rider may change position within the lane to improve visibility or.
cards.back: A rider may change position within the lane to improve visibility or avoid a hazard. That position change alone does not establish an intention to turn.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Potholes, gravel, slippery surfaces, seams, rail crossings and grooved pavement.
cards.back: Potholes, gravel, slippery surfaces, seams, rail crossings and grooved pavement may cause a rider to change speed or lane position suddenly.

decks.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Before entering a motorcycle's path, make sure the rider's maneuver has actually.
cards.back: Before entering a motorcycle's path, make sure the rider's maneuver has actually begun. A motorcycle's flashing signal may have been left on rather than indicating the next turn.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The handbook recommends a following interval of three or four.
cards.back: The handbook recommends a following interval of three or four seconds behind a motorcycle, with additional space to avoid abrupt braking.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: When a motorcycle passes your vehicle, maintain lane position and speed to.
cards.back: When a motorcycle passes your vehicle, maintain lane position and speed to let the rider complete the pass and regain a normal lane position.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: When passing a motorcycle, use a full adjacent lane and leave.
cards.back: When passing a motorcycle, use a full adjacent lane and leave enough room before returning so the rider is not forced to swerve.

decks.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Traffic approaching a school bus stopped for loading or unloading generally must.
cards.back: Traffic approaching a school bus stopped for loading or unloading generally must stop. With a dividing median, opposite-side traffic is excepted, while traffic following or beside the bus in its direction must stop.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: After stopping for a school bus, wait until it resumes moving or.
cards.back: After stopping for a school bus, wait until it resumes moving or deactivates the warnings, and until all passengers loading or unloading have cleared the roadway.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Large trucks are longer, heavier and harder to.
cards.back: Large trucks are longer, heavier and harder to maneuver than cars and require additional room for turning.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The handbook calls a truck or bus's enlarged blind areas.
cards.back: The handbook calls a truck or bus's enlarged blind areas the no-zones, including areas beside, behind and in front of it.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Before towing, use suitable equipment, stay within the.
cards.back: Before towing, use suitable equipment, stay within the towing capacity, distribute weight appropriately and secure the load.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Inspect and maintain both tow vehicle and trailer, become familiar with.
cards.back: Inspect and maintain both tow vehicle and trailer, become familiar with handling through practice, and consider tow mirrors or other needed safety equipment.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Allow time when trailering and remain calm if control is.
cards.back: Allow time when trailering and remain calm if control is lost; the handbook's brief checklist is not a complete towing procedure.

decks.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A truck or bus has large blind areas on both sides. If.
cards.back: A truck or bus has large blind areas on both sides. If its driver's face is not visible in the side mirror, do not assume the driver can see your vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The right-side blind area is especially hazardous because.
cards.back: The right-side blind area is especially hazardous because large vehicles may need a wide right turn.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Avoid following closely in a large vehicle's rear blind area; you.
cards.back: Avoid following closely in a large vehicle's rear blind area; you may be unseen and unable to see traffic conditions ahead of it.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Large vehicles need extra stopping room. Do not merge closely.
cards.back: Large vehicles need extra stopping room. Do not merge closely in front of a truck or bus and then reduce speed.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Before moving into the lane ahead of a truck or bus.
cards.back: Before moving into the lane ahead of a truck or bus, make sure its entire front is visible in your rearview mirror.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Give a commercial vehicle ample space during highway entry and.
cards.back: Give a commercial vehicle ample space during highway entry and merging, and avoid cutting it off, tailgating or speeding around it.
